Team — forwarding Crestline's ask. Quick summary and suggested positions:

1) Audit rights: Crestline requests either an on-site one-time audit or remote evidence review. Our standard: remote evidence review + annual SOC 2 + scoped security questionnaire. On-site audits are high-cost/rare; propose: offer a remote review + right to request an on-site audit with commercial terms (cost recovery + 60 days notice) — acceptability: medium.

2) Subprocessors: they want "30-day notice" before new subprocessors. We typically provide 30-day notice for major changes, but for critical infra changes our ops flow may lead to shorter windows. Proposed compromise: 30-day notice + ability to notify sooner for emergency capacity with post-facto notice and mitigation info.

3) International transfers: we use SCCs where required and customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For hosted customers, confirm SCCs + encryption in transit and at rest; for Crestline let's propose SCCs + description of encryption/KMS.

4) Evidence: we'll provide SOC 2 Type II (redacted) and pen test executive summary (no raw findings).

Ask: Aditya, can you run a legal redline for the attached Crestline document and mark any non-starters? Aisha, can you confirm what we can provide for on-site audit logistics / cost estimate if needed? Laura, I'll need a short SOC2 & pen test stub to attach to the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — aiming to get this buttoned by EOD Tue for DocuSign execution mid-week.

Marissa / team — reviewed Crestline's redline. High-level positions and proposed edits (see inline comments in drive doc):

- Audit rights: we should avoid open-ended on-site audit language. Proposed language: "Customer may request a one-time on-site audit subject to reasonable scope, 60 days' advance notice, and Customer bears reasonable travel and third-party audit fees; alternatively, Customer may perform a remote evidence review." This preserves our security posture and limits operational impact.

- Subprocessors: 30 days' notice is acceptable for non-critical additions. For critical infra (e.g., new GPU provider or networking vendor) we need emergency exception language. Proposed: "We will provide at least 30 days' notice for planned additions; where immediate changes are required for security or continuity, we will provide notice as soon as practicable and document mitigation steps."

- Data transfers: we confirm use of EU SCCs for GDPR transfers. For hosted customers we also offer encryption at rest and in transit; provide summary of KMS options (Redwood-managed KMS vs customer-managed in Dedicated/Private).

- Evidence: we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and an executive summary of the most recent penetration test. We should avoid sharing raw test logs or vulnerability exploit code.

- Signature: recommend executing via DocuSign. Once Crestline accepts our redline, we attach the redacted SOC2 + pen-test exec summary to the envelope.

Non-starters (flagged):
- Unlimited audit rights or broad forensic data access.
- Requirement to provide full pen test raw data.
- Indemnity language tied to subprocessors' actions beyond standard warranty/limitations.

I'll prepare a redline (v3) and upload to the shared drive. Marissa: if you can confirm they're ok with the on-site cost recovery language, I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope. Aisha: please confirm whether we can host a remote evidence review with a secure view-only session and the typical checklist (SOC2 + infra diagrams + config screenshots).
